TI An Examination of Pre-Service Teachers' Awareness of Online Privacy in
   Relation to Various Variables
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Online Privacy; Awareness; Cyber Security; Pre-service teacher
ID LITERACY; STUDENTS
AB This study aimed to investigate pre-service teachers' awareness of online privacy in relation to various demographic and experiential variables. The study used the survey model, a quantitative research method. The study sample consisted of 218 pre-service teachers studying in seven different undergraduate programs in the Faculty of Education of a state university. Data were collected online via a form comprising three sections. In addition to descriptive statistical analysis, independent samples t-tests, oneway ANOVA, and Pearson correlation tests were conducted. According to the study results, no significant relationship was found between online privacy awareness and gender. Enrolling in a media literacy course positively affected online privacy awareness. Participants who neither encountered online privacy risks nor violated others' privacy reported higher levels of awareness. Participants' Internet usage time did not significantly affect their online privacy awareness. Moreover, the study identified a significant and positive relationship between online privacy awareness and cybersecurity perception. Future studies may investigate how preservice teachers' online privacy and cybersecurity awareness relate to their school experience and teaching practice performance.

TI The Role of Dispositions and Metacognitive Experiences in the Process of
   Solving Mathematical Problems
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Dispositions; Metacognitive Experiences; Problem-Solving Skills;
   Scenario Based Mathematic; Problems
ID CRITICAL THINKING DISPOSITION; DIFFICULTY; KNOWLEDGE; VIEW
AB This study investigated the dispositions exhibited by 10th grade students while solving scenario-based mathematics problems, the metacognitive experiences they possess, and whether these differed according to the academic level of the schools they attended. Conducted using the phenomenology design, one of the qualitative research approaches, the participants were determined using the maximum diversity sampling technique, one of the purposive sampling methods. Qualitative interviews were conducted with one 10th-grade student selected from each of ten different secondary education institutions with varying academic levels in Istanbul during the 2022-2023 academic years. The data collection tools included a semi-structured interview form, an observation form, and two scenario-based mathematics problems developed by the researcher. The obtained data was analyzed using content analysis. The findings of the study revealed that the participants who exhibited certain dispositions simultaneously had higher problem-solving skills compared to those who displayed these dispositions individually. Additionally, it was found that if the exhibited dispositions were not supported by the disposition of being careful, they could be ineffective in problem-solving skills, and the self-confidence disposition negatively impacted problem-solving abilities in some cases. Furthermore, the findings demonstrated that mathematical prejudice as part of metacognitive experience could hinder problem-solving ability, while enjoying mathematics functioned as a motivational factor in displaying problem-solving skills, whereas disliking mathematics negatively influenced these skills.

TI Developing the Divorce Anxiety Scale: Validity and Reliability Study
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Divorce; Divorce Anxiety; Marriage; Scale Development
ID CONFLICT; TERM
AB Within the scope of this study, the concept of divorce anxiety, which has not been mentioned much in the literature before, was explained and the Divorce Anxiety Scale developed to help reveal this construct, was subjected to validity and reliability analyses. The concept of divorce anxiety can be defined as the anxiety that individuals feel about the changes and uncertainties that may occur at the end of their marital relationship. Two different study groups were reached within the scope of the research. The first study group consisted of 430 individuals and structural validity studies were conducted with the data obtained. The findings revealed a three-factor structure that accounted for 70% of the explained variance. Forthe validity and reliability studies ofthe emerging structure, data were collected from the second study group consisting of 390 individuals. The findings of the confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) revealed that the model related to the construct showed good and excellent fit (qs/df=3.25; GFI=0.88; AGFI=0.84; NNFI=0.96; NFI=0.96; CFI=0.97; RMSEA=0.07). In addition to the CFA findings, convergent and divergent validity calculations related to the scale were also conducted. The findings demonstrated that the scale meets both convergent and divergent validity conditions, confirming that it is a statistically valid and reliable measurement tool.

TI Development of an Algorithmic Thinking Scale Based on the Futschek Model
   in Mathematics Education
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Algorithmic Thinking; Problem Solving; Algorithm; Scale Development;
   Mathematics Education
ID STUDENTS; INSTRUCTION; RELIABILITY
AB The aim of the study is to develop a valid and reliable algorithmic thinking scale that can assess cognitive processes such as understanding the problem, creating a solution path, developing strategies, identifying errors, making a solution plan, and evaluating during the process of solving mathematical problems. Based on a review of the literature literature and Futschek's algorithmic thinking process model the researchers designed a draft scale consisting of 42 items on a five-point Likert. The developed draft scale was applied to a total of 533 students, including 312 female and 221 male ninth-grade students, in three different high schools in the Kapakl & imath; district of Tekirda & gbreve; province during the 2024-2025 academic year. In the analysis of the data, SPSS 27 and AMOS 24 were used to determine item-total test correlations, Cronbach's Alpha reliability, Spearman-Brown Prophecy reliability, composite reliability, and test-retest reliability coefficients. In addition, hypothesis testings, exploratory factor analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis were performed. As a result of the analyses and expert evaluations, the scale was reduced to 25 items to form the final scale. In conclusion, it can be said that the developed scale is expected contribute as a comprehensive and functional measurement tool to measure the difficulties students experience in the problem-solving processes, their preferences in the decision-making stages, the effectiveness of their strategy use, and their levels of algorithmic competence and awareness.
